resources.string: Your Synapse server at a glance: who\'s signed in, health and what needs attention.
Add your Synapse server to get started.
SynapseCtrl is free and open source. Sponsor development on GitHub
Found a problem or have an idea? Open an issue on GitHub

Enter the address of your Synapse server and sign in with an account that is a server admin. If /_synapse/admin is only open on your network, use Synapse\'s LAN address, like http://192.168.1.20:8008.
Connects to %1$s, and only to this address
Without http://, SynapseCtrl uses HTTPS. SynapseCtrl only ever connects to the address you enter here.
That doesn\'t look like a web address.

Plain http:// is only allowed for addresses on your own network (like 192.168.x.x, synapse.lan or a Tailscale address), because SynapseCtrl sends your admin access token with every request. Use https:// for this address.
Defaults to the server name, like vkhub.org
Allow plain HTTP for this server
Your admin access token travels unencrypted on your network

Only for addresses on your own network or your Tailscale tailnet. A name like synapse.lan or synapse.tailnet-name.ts.net must also point to a private address, or SynapseCtrl won\'t connect. HTTPS is safer.

SynapseCtrl will talk to %1$s without encryption. Every request carries your admin access token, which can do anything on your server, so anyone who can watch your network could take it over. Only do this on a network you trust.
%1$s uses a certificate your phone doesn\'t know, like a self-signed certificate.
%1$s now presents a different certificate from the one you trusted. Only continue if you replaced or renewed it yourself.
Check that this SHA-256 fingerprint matches your certificate (on the server: openssl x509 -in cert.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha256):
From now on SynapseCtrl only accepts this exact certificate from this server.
Switch, add or remove Synapse servers
SynapseCtrl logs its access token out on the server (so it stops working there too), then forgets this server and deletes the token from the phone. Nothing else changes on the server.
Hide every action that changes something on this server, and refuse to send one
Can\'t reach %1$s. Check the address and that your phone is on a network that can reach it.
%1$s presents a different certificate from the one you trusted. SynapseCtrl stopped connecting to protect your access token.
Wrong username or password, or the server refused the login.
%1$s answered with a redirect. SynapseCtrl never follows redirects, so enter the address Synapse actually answers on (often its https:// address).
%1$s redirects to %2$s. SynapseCtrl never follows redirects, so enter that address instead (often the https:// one).
SynapseCtrl won\'t use plain HTTP for %1$s: it\'s only allowed for addresses on your own network, with the server\'s HTTP switch on.
SynapseCtrl only connects to the servers you added, so this request wasn\'t sent.
This server is in read-only mode, so nothing was changed. Turn read-only mode off to make changes.
Cancelled: the change wasn\'t confirmed with your fingerprint or app PIN, so nothing was sent.

Ask for an app PIN (and optionally your fingerprint) when opening SynapseCtrl. While locked, your admin access tokens stay encrypted with the PIN and nothing is sent to your servers, unless you turned on background checks
SynapseCtrl has no analytics or tracking. It only talks to your own Synapse servers.

Background checks are on, so they can still reach your servers while SynapseCtrl is locked: your admin access tokens are then only encrypted with the Android Keystore, as without the app lock. Turn off background checks in Notifications to keep them sealed with your PIN too. SynapseCtrl has no analytics or tracking.
Screenshots and screen recordings show a blank screen
The recent apps view shows a blank card instead of the app
Couldn\'t unlock with your fingerprint. Use your PIN.
A fingerprint was added or removed. Unlock with your PIN, then turn fingerprint unlock on again.
Enter your PIN. It\'s needed after a restart and every 72 hours.
Too many tries. Try again in %1$d s

The PIN can\'t be recovered, because it encrypts your saved access tokens. SynapseCtrl will remove every server with its token. The tokens stay valid on the server until you log them out there (for example from the admin account\'s session list). Nothing else changes on your servers.
At least %1$d digits, different from your phone\'s PIN. If you forget it, the only way back in is to add your servers again.
At least %1$d digits, different from your phone\'s PIN.
At least %1$d digits, separate from your phone\'s PIN
Enter your app PIN to turn the lock off.
Too easy to guess. Try a less obvious PIN.
The PINs didn\'t match. Start again.
Couldn\'t save the PIN. Try again.
Only strong biometrics such as your fingerprint, checked by the phone\'s secure hardware. The PIN is still needed after a restart and every 72 hours.
Set up a fingerprint on this phone first
As soon as you leave the app
Ask for your fingerprint or app PIN before anything that changes a server: users, invites, rooms, media and reports. Once confirmed, the next minute doesn\'t ask again
SynapseCtrl is about to change something on your server
SynapseCtrl is about to change something on your server. Enter your app PIN or use your fingerprint.
Background checks, push through ntfy, what to notify about
Notifications are blocked: tap to allow them

Synapse can\'t send notifications itself, so SynapseCtrl checks your servers in the background and tells you about new event reports, health checks that start failing (discovery, federation, calls), servers that can\'t be reached, new users and media storage over a limit. Push through ntfy can start that check at once. The checks only read; nothing changes on your servers.
Notifications are blocked for SynapseCtrl, so the background checks can\'t tell you anything.
Looks at every saved server and notifies about new problems

Android runs background checks at most every 15 minutes, and can delay them to save battery. They only talk to your own Synapse servers. With the app lock on, your admin access tokens stay usable in the background while these checks are on (see Privacy and security).
Last check %1$s couldn\'t reach the server
New reports, failing health checks, unreachable servers and new users are on as soon as background checks are. The media limit is up to you.
Two checks in a row couldn\'t reach Synapse, or its access token or admin access stopped working
SynapseCtrl may run in the background
Battery optimisation can delay or skip checks

On ColorOS (OPPO, OnePlus) and other phones that close background apps aggressively: open SynapseCtrl\'s app info, then under Battery choose Allow background activity (or Don\'t optimise), and allow Auto launch if your phone has it.
New reports, unreachable servers and media storage
Something on your Synapse server needs a look. Unlock to see it.
Runs the background check right away whenever something posts to SynapseCtrl\'s push address

Synapse can\'t push anything itself. Turn this on, copy the push address and let something on your network post to it, like a cron job. Every push makes SynapseCtrl check your servers at once, at most once a minute; what the message says is ignored. The regular background checks keep running as well.
ntfy isn\'t installed. Push comes only through the ntfy app: install it, connect it to your ntfy server, then come back here. Background checks work without it.
Turn on Check in the background too: a push only starts that check.
ntfy couldn\'t register SynapseCtrl (%1$s). Open ntfy once, then try again.
ntfy temporarily unavailable: its server can\'t be reached. The push address stays the same and background checks keep running.
Tap to copy. Treat this address like a password: anyone who has it can make SynapseCtrl check your servers (it never changes anything on them).
Android can cut ntfy\'s connection while the phone sleeps, so pushes arrive late. Tap to open ntfy\'s app info and set Battery to Unrestricted.
Local accounts: create, reset passwords, admins, devices, deactivate.
Rooms on your server: members, block, delete.
Storage per user, cleaning up local and remote media, quarantine.
Used once to log in: SynapseCtrl gets its own access token and never stores the password
Leave empty to keep the current sign-in
From an admin account. It will be logged out when you remove this server, so don\'t paste the token your chat app uses.
Read-only mode hides every write action and refuses to send one, even if a screen still shows it.
%1$s was removed, but its access token couldn\'t be logged out on the server. Log it out there yourself (the \"SynapseCtrl (Android)\" device of your admin account).
The access token doesn\'t work any more (logged out or expired). Sign in again.
This account isn\'t a server admin. Make it one on the server (see the README), or sign in with an admin account.
%1$s answers, but not on /_synapse/admin (HTTP %2$d). If you restricted the admin API to your network, use Synapse\'s LAN address here, like http://192.168.1.20:8008.
%1$s doesn\'t offer password login (it may use single sign-on or Matrix Authentication Service). Paste an access token from an admin account instead.
%1$s answered, but not like Synapse. Check the address: it should be where Synapse itself answers.
Not found: it may have been deleted already.
Synapse is rate-limiting these requests. Wait a moment and try again.
People can only sign up with a token when registration_requires_token is on in homeserver.yaml (with enable_registration). Tap a token to change or delete it.
Leave empty for a random one. Letters, digits and . _ ~ -, up to 64
Only letters, digits and . _ ~ -, up to 64 characters
Nobody can sign up with it any more. Accounts already made with it stay.

You're invited to my Matrix server, %1$s.

Registration token: %2$s

How to sign up:
1. Install ChatCtrl (from the CtrlF-Droid repo) or any Matrix app, like Element X.
2. Choose Create account, and enter %3$s as the server.
3. Pick a username and password, and enter the registration token when asked.
Totals cover the 100 users with the most media.
Copies of files from other servers. Purging only frees space: they\'re downloaded again when someone opens them.
Delete copies from other servers nobody opened lately
Copies of media from other servers that nobody opened for %1$s are deleted from your server. They\'re downloaded again if someone opens them.
Files uploaded by people on your server. Synapse decides by when a file was last opened, not when it was uploaded. Deleted files are gone for good: messages that show them get a broken image.
Don\'t delete avatars of people and rooms
Counts what would be deleted first
Local media not opened for %1$s and larger than %2$s will be deleted from your server for good.
About %1$s files (%2$s) match. Synapse has no dry run, so this is counted from each user\'s media list.
At least %1$s files (%2$s) match (counted from the first part of the media lists). Synapse has no dry run.
The number of matching files couldn\'t be counted.
Profile pictures and room avatars are kept.
Profile pictures and room avatars are deleted too.
Quarantined media stops being served to anyone, but stays on disk. For a whole room or user, use their page.
One file, from your server or another
Paste an mxc:// address, or a media ID from your own server.
Stop serving this file to anyone
This user hasn\'t uploaded anything to your server.
Remove it from your server for good
This file (%1$s) and its thumbnails are deleted from your server for good. Messages that show it get a broken image or link.
A server notice arrives as a message from your server in a special room the user can\'t leave or reply to. Good for maintenance announcements.

Synapse only sends notices when server_notices is set up in homeserver.yaml (system_mxid_localpart and a room name). If it isn\'t, you\'ll see Synapse\'s error. Everyone means every active local user except bots and bridges, one notice each.
Someone on your server reported a message
Client or server discovery, federation or calls (MatrixRTC) stopped working
Someone signed up with a registration token, or an account was created
Local media grew past the size you set
Over your limit of %1$s. Clean up old media on the Media tab.
Open Reports in SynapseCtrl to look at it.
A new account was created on your server.
Reported messages waiting for a look
Over your limit of %1$s (set it in Notifications)
Checked from your phone against your server\'s public addresses, without any outside tester. Pull down to check again.
The admin API answers at the address saved in SynapseCtrl
/.well-known/matrix/client points apps to your server, and it answers
/.well-known/matrix/client names a server, but that address doesn\'t answer like Synapse
/.well-known/matrix/client is missing or wrong, so apps can\'t find your server from your user IDs
/.well-known/matrix/server tells other servers where to reach yours
No /.well-known/matrix/server: other servers try port 8448 on your server name
Other servers can reach yours: it answers with its version and signing keys
Your server answers other servers, but its signing keys don\'t match its name
Other servers can\'t reach yours where discovery points them
Client discovery lists your LiveKit service, and it answers
Your LiveKit service answers with an error
No working LiveKit service: calls in Element X won\'t connect
Registration tokens, and sharing an invite
The servers yours talks to, and resetting failed connections
Send a message to one user or to everyone
When someone on your server reports a message, it shows up here.
From -100 (most offensive) to 0, if the reporter\'s app set one
Reports about a whole account, rather than one message, show up here.
Shadow-ban, suspend or deactivate from there
Remove it from the list once handled
The report is removed. Nothing happens to the message or the people involved.
Synapse didn\'t return the reported event (it may have been deleted).
To act on the sender, open their account: shadow-ban, suspend or deactivate are there. To remove the message, a room moderator redacts it in a chat app.
Servers your server has talked to over federation show up here.

Failing servers are shown first. Synapse waits longer and longer between tries; tap a failing server to reset that, so it tries again on the next message. Errors can take up to 20 minutes to show here.
Synapse forgets the failures and the waiting time, and tries this server again as soon as there\'s something to send. Use it after the other server is back up.
Search name, alias or room ID
No room matches this search and filter.
Blocked by %1$s: nobody can join it.
Only for people on this server
People on your server come first; tap one to manage the account.
Gives your admin account the highest power level in this room
Synapse joins %1$s to this room (or invites it, if needed) with the highest power level, using a local member who already has it. Other members see this in the room.
Kicks a local member, as your admin account

The admin API can\'t remove people from rooms, so this is a normal kick by your admin account. It only works if your account is in the room with enough power: use Make me room admin first. They can join again unless the room is invite-only.
Nobody on your server can join it
Nobody on your server can join it from now on. People already in it stay, and nothing is deleted.
People on your server can join it again.
Every file shared in this room stops being served
Quarantine all media in this room?
All local and remote media in this room stops being served to anyone. Protected media is skipped. The files stay on disk.
Remove everyone from your server and delete it
Deleting a room can\'t be undone. It runs in the background on the server; SynapseCtrl shows its progress.
The %1$d members from your server are removed from the room, and its history is deleted from your server. People on other servers keep their copy.
Nobody on your server can join it again
Remove every trace of it from the database
Move members to a new room
A new room made by %1$s, with a message saying what happened
Couldn\'t check the progress just now; trying again.
This can\'t be undone. Type this to confirm:
Nobody matches this search and filter.
This is the account SynapseCtrl is signed in with, so admin rights, bans, locking and deactivation aren\'t offered here.
Leave empty to remove the display name.
An override replaces the server\'s message rate limit for this user only. Both values at 0 turns rate limiting off for them, for bots and bridges.
How many actions per second this user may do, and how many in a burst before the limit applies. 0 and 0 means no limit.
Set a new password for this user
Set a new password for %1$s. Give it to them yourself; Synapse doesn\'t send it anywhere.
Full access to the admin API and everything on the server
They get full access to the admin API: every user, room and setting on the server, like you have.
They lose access to the admin API. Their account and rooms stay as they are.
Their messages quietly stop reaching anyone, without them knowing

Their requests still seem to work, but what they send no longer reaches rooms or other users. Use it as a last resort: their apps can behave strangely, and kicking or banning from rooms is usually better.
What they send reaches rooms and people again.
Can read, but can\'t send, join, invite or change their profile
They can still sign in and read, but can\'t send messages, join or knock on rooms, invite people, change their profile or redact other people\'s messages. You can lift it again.
They can send, join and invite again.
Can\'t use the account until it\'s unlocked
Their sessions stop working until you unlock the account. Nothing is deleted.
They can use their account again.
All %1$d devices are logged out and their access tokens stop working. Their end-to-end encryption keys on those devices are lost unless they set up key backup.
Device %1$s is logged out and its access token stops working.
A message from the server to this user
Every file they uploaded stops being served
Every file this user uploaded to your server stops being served to anyone. The files stay on disk, and you can lift the quarantine per file later.
Deactivating can\'t be undone: the user is logged out everywhere, removed from every room, and their password, devices, encryption keys and email addresses are deleted.
They\'re logged out everywhere and removed from every room. Their password, devices, encryption keys, email addresses and account data are deleted. Their messages and uploaded media stay.
Also removes their display name, avatar and profile, and marks them erased: their messages stay visible to people who were in the room, but are hidden from anyone who joins later.
It can\'t sign in, and it isn\'t in any rooms
SynapseCtrl doesn\'t reactivate accounts: a reactivated account has no password or rooms, so it\'s cleaner to create a new one.
Only lowercase letters, digits and . _ = - / + are allowed
At least 8 characters. Copy it before you create the account: it isn\'t shown again.
Only make someone a server admin if they need to manage the server too.
The account works right away. Give the user ID and password to the person yourself; they can sign in with ChatCtrl or any Matrix app and change the password there.
Your Synapse server online or not, active users and open reports
Unlock the app to see your server
